case_reviews.model_answer:
Totally fair to feel a bit anxious—but the good news is you're already set up better than you think. You have a Suica card, you're in Shinjuku (which is one of the easiest hubs to navigate from), and the train system is genuinely well-signposted, with English signage at most major stations.

A few tips grounded in your actual plans:

**Your Suica is your best friend.** It works across JR, Tokyo Metro, Toei lines, and even on many buses and convenience-store purchases. You don't need to buy separate tickets for anything. Just tap in and out. If your Suica runs low, you can charge it at any ticket machine—most have an English mode.

**For Tsukiji specifically:** you already have a good route (JR Yamanote Line to Shimbashi, then Ginza Line to Tsukijishijo). If you go early morning as planned, trains are less crowded and direction is easy to follow. Just note that "Tsukijishijo Station" is the one right by the market area—there's also an "Tsukiji Station" on the Oedo Line if you ever take that instead, so don't mix them up.

**Give yourself one extra transfer cushion.** When you're anxious, rushing makes it worse. 30–40 minutes is the estimate; budget 50. If you miss a train, another comes in 2–5 minutes anyway.

**Money exchange:** it's worth checking rates at a proper exchange counter rather than a hotel—Shinjuku has several, and many ATMs at 7-Eleven or Japan Post accept foreign cards and dispense yen directly. That's often the easiest and gives decent rates.

**General ground rules that keep stress low:**
- Station staff are used to tourists; asking is normal and they're usually helpful.
- Google Maps works well for train routing in Tokyo, including platform numbers and exit numbers.
- All major stations have English signage, but smaller ones may not—have your destination written in Japanese on your phone to show someone if needed.
- Pickpocket-style worry in Tokyo is mostly overblown, but keep your Suica and cash somewhere you won't fumble for.

The first day is the hardest. After one or two trips you'll stop thinking about it.
case_reviews.question: I’m a bit anxious about getting around Tokyo. Do you have any helpful tips?
